questions.q: What grain does gold.FactOrders use, and why?
options: One row per order line, matching the legacy order system's natural grain, since that's the finest-grained fact the warehouse needs to support
One row per customer, decided independently of any source system
One row per day across all customers, aggregated immediately
The grain is left undefined until the dashboard queries the table
questions.explain: Lesson 8's grain-first principle applies again here: the fact table's grain is fixed to match the finest-grained data actually needed, one order line at a time.

questions.q: Why do DimCustomer and DimProduct reference the crosswalk rather than copying data directly from a single source?
options: They are conformed dimensions — built from the crosswalk so the three-system disagreement about identity is already resolved before any fact row loads
Copying directly from a single source is actually what happens, and the crosswalk is unused at this stage
DimCustomer and DimProduct are not dimensions at all in this schema
The crosswalk is only used for the fact table, not for dimension tables
questions.explain: The whole point of Lesson 71's crosswalk is to resolve customer/product identity upstream so every foreign key in FactOrders points at something already conformed.

questions.q: Why must FactOrders load only after DimCustomer and DimProduct have finished loading?
options: Writing an order-line row requires a valid customer_key and product_key, which only exist once the dimension loads have resolved every reference through the crosswalk
There is no real dependency — the load order is arbitrary and only a convention
FactOrders contains no foreign keys, so dimension load order is irrelevant
DimCustomer and DimProduct actually depend on FactOrders loading first
questions.explain: This is a hard load dependency, not just a timing preference — FactOrders cannot be written correctly without valid conformed keys already in place.

questions.q: How does this project's conforming work differ from Project 1's, even though both use the same star schema idea?
options: Project 1 conformed two feeds from the same organization in silver; Project 2 conforms three systems that were never designed to talk to each other, requiring the crosswalk to be correct before any fact loads
Project 2 does not use a star schema at all, unlike Project 1
Both projects conform data in exactly the same way with no meaningful difference
Project 1's conforming work happened after fact table loads, unlike Project 2's
questions.explain: The modeling idea (fact table, fixed grain, conformed dimensions) is identical across both projects — only where and how hard the conforming work is differs.

questions.q: What does the reconciliation check now verify, using the tables built in this lesson?
options: That SUM(order_total) in gold.FactOrders matches the legacy system's total for the same date, within tolerance, every night during the coexistence period
That gold.DimCustomer has more rows than gold.DimProduct
That the Fabric Data Warehouse costs less to run than the legacy SQL Server instance
That FactOrders loads before both of its dimension tables
questions.explain: Lesson 71 planned this reconciliation check; this lesson gives it real tables to compare against before cutover is approved.
